caveats.note: topics passed as parameters, runtime variables or env vars - and constants that are ambiguous, or lower-case bindings in another file - are extracted as an unresolved framework tag (`unresolved:<framework>`, one per framework and direction, anchored at every such call site, also where the same call form names a literal topic elsewhere in the file) and never paired; literal constants the repo table resolves are folded. Outside NATS, a topic built by a call (`topicFor(id)`) in a file that names another topic of the same framework is not recorded, and a concatenation is read as its leading literal (`'audit.' + id` is `audit.`). Go nats.go / JetStream calls are read on any receiver in a file importing the library, except a receiver the file declares with another library's type and, in a file that also imports another broker library, a receiver the file does not declare as NATS; the receiver's type is read from the file's text, so a `type Conn = nats.Conn` alias or an embedded `*nats.Conn` reads as another type, and in a nats.go-only file an undeclared receiver's `.Publish(` reads as NATS; `.Request(` / `.RequestMsg(`, `FilterSubjects`, `ConsumerConfig{FilterSubject}` and the jetstream `Consume` / `Messages` / `Fetch` API are not read. A NATS publish subject built from literal tokens and whole dynamic tokens (`+`, an interpolated literal, Go `fmt.Sprintf`, a same-file Go function whose body only returns it) is read with `*` for each dynamic token (`"shop.shipments." + id` is `shop.shipments.*`) and pairs only wildcard subscriptions (Weak); a dynamic piece inside a token (`"orders-" + region`), a concatenation led by a constant (`PREFIX + "." + id`), a subject built across statements, a subject function that is a method, lives in another file or does more than return, Java `String.format`, Python `%` / `.format()`, Elixir `<>`, a subscriber subject built at run time and a format read from a struct field or an env default (`fmt.Sprintf(p.template, id)`) are the unresolved tag; an overlay `[constants]` pin of the expression as written (`"p.template" = "shop.orders.%s.placed"`) folds it
caveats.verify: grep the topic constant or env var name

GCP Pub/Sub subscribers name a subscription, not a topic: a subscriber pairs with a topic's publishers when both name the topic, or when a Terraform `google_pubsub_subscription` of the same repo binds its subscription to the topic (`topic = "orders"` or `projects/

/topics/orders`, or a `google_pubsub_topic..name` / `.id` reference; DERIVED, Medium, rule binding). A subscription created in code (`create_subscription`) or by gcloud / the console, a Terraform subscription name or topic that is interpolated (`"${var.env}-orders"`) or read from a variable or a module output (`var.topic`, `module.x.name`), a topic resource declared in another repo of the build, and a subscription bound to two topics pair nothing

caveats.note: GraphQL SDL embedded in code is read only from a GraphQL-marked literal: a gql / graphql tag or call, a buildSchema / MustParseSchema / ParseSchema / from_definition argument, a /* GraphQL */ or #graphql literal, a GRAPHQL / GQL heredoc, or a literal bound to a variable or key named typeDefs / type_defs. SDL kept unmarked in a differently named variable (a plain template in `const schema = ...`, a Go string passed to MustParseSchema by name) is not read: its root types and fields mint no GRAPHQL_RESOLVER, so its clients' operations pair with nothing. `.graphql` / `.graphqls` / `.gql` files are read whole. An operation pairs with the resolvers of the root fields its document selects (an alias reads its field, `__typename` is skipped, an inline fragment's fields count, a fragment spread's do not), whatever root type declares them (`query { orders }` pairs an `orders` only Subscription declares); an operation whose document gives no root field (a generated hook, a document built at run time or selecting only fragment spreads) pairs by its operation name; a document that is, or starts with, a `${FRAGMENT}` interpolation mints no operation; and an operation read at a hook or client call (`useQuery(DOC)`) takes the name and fields of the file's first gql document, not necessarily the one it passes. A TS client's http(s) or root-relative `uri` / `url` (Apollo ApolloClient / HttpLink / createHttpLink, urql createClient / new Client, graphql-request GraphQLClient), or a `${..}` / config-member URL through the endpoint fold, mints the transport `endpoint:POST:<path>` (GET too when the client sends queries by GET) that the HTTP resolver pairs with the server's route; a ws:// URL, a graphql-ws client and apollo-angular's `httpLink.create` mint none; an unpaired transport whose project's operations pair a resolver on a server holding no route at its last path segment is no unpaired_endpoint. A client's base URL narrows its project's operations to one server only when it is one literal absolute URL (Apollo `uri`, HttpLink / createHttpLink, urql createClient / new Client, graphql-request GraphQLClient) whose host names a nested project or an IaC service; a relative, env-var or interpolated URL leaves an operation paired with every server that declares the field. An operation whose every client URL is a literal public host (a dotted DNS name: not localhost, an IP, an internal TLD or a documentation domain) that no configuration constant of the repo names (a SCREAMING_CASE or dotted key, a `.glia/overlay.toml [constants]` pin) and that names no project or IaC service of the build is external (its ENDPOINT_HIT carries `"external":true`) and pairs with no server, even one declaring the field; a client with one host-less or internal site still pairs.
caveats.verify: grep 'type Query {' / 'type Mutation {' outside .graphql / .graphqls / .gql files and read the variable that holds it; for an operation paired with several servers, or with none, read the client's uri / url

caveats.note: a WebSocket upgrade whose route is registered more than one call away from the upgrading function, or through a router glia does not extract, stays unpaired; a client whose URL has no static path is not paired; a client URL is read from the call, from a `const` (Dart `final` / `const`, Go `:=` / `const`) of an enclosing scope at most 40 lines above it, from the file's one `readonly` field of that name, from a URL builder given one literal path (`buildWsUrl('api/chat/ws')`, Weak) or from Go `url.URL{Path: ..}`, and a `let` / `var` / reassigned or parameter URL is not read; a `${..}` base or a whole-URL config member the repo const table binds once folds to its path and host, while a base bound per deployment (environment.ts and environment.prod.ts) or read from `process.env` does not; a route whose path a client paired through its upgrade handler is no unpaired_route; a client matching several same-path handlers narrows to one service only when its URL's static head carries a literal host naming a nested project or an IaC service (compose / Kubernetes service, deployment, statefulset, image), otherwise it pairs with all of them; a client whose every site dials a literal public host (a dotted DNS name: not localhost, an IP, an internal TLD or a documentation domain) that no configuration constant of the repo names and that names no project or IaC service of the build is external (its ENDPOINT_HIT carries `"external":true`) and pairs with no handler, even one of the same path; a client with one host-less or internal site still pairs
caveats.verify: grep the upgrade call and the route registration; for a client paired with several handlers, or with none, read its URL
